currentContext.business: The Company continues to operate in the textile trading business, primarily engaged in the trading of cloth and grey fabrics, which remains its principal line of business. During FY2025-26 the Members approved, by Special Resolution at the AGM held on 16th September 2025, an alteration of Clause III(A) (Main Objects) of the Memorandum of Association to broaden the scope of activities to include, inter alia, furniture and interior solutions, human and pet nutrition products, solar and renewable energy solutions, cosmetics and personal care products, advertising and media services, artist and event management, and information technology and software development services. Management states it will evaluate these opportunities from time to time based on market conditions and commercial viability while continuing to strengthen existing textile trading operations; no operations in the newly added objects are described as having commenced.

Newly enabled objects (not described as: Information technology and software development services

currentContext.strategies: Continue the existing textile trading business — trading of cloth and grey fabrics — as the principal line of business while strengthening those operations.|Hold optionality across newly permitted sectors: having altered Clause III(A) (Main Objects) of the MoA by Special Resolution at the AGM of 16th September 2025, evaluate entry into furniture and interior solutions, human and pet nutrition products, solar and renewable energy solutions, cosmetics and personal care products, advertising and media services, artist and event management, and IT/software development services 'as and when considered commercially viable'.|Build a diversified business model that management argues gives resilience against sector-specific risks: 'The diversified nature of the Company's business objectives provides resilience against sector-specific risks while enabling sustainable long-term growth.'|Strengthen internal systems, internal financial controls and the risk-management framework, and maintain full regulatory compliance, as the stated basis for growth.
currentContext.expansion: The annual report describes no capital-expenditure project, no plant, no capacity addition and no commissioning or ramp-up of any kind. The only expansion event of FY2025-26 is a legal one: at the Annual General Meeting held on 16th September 2025 the Members, by Special Resolution under Section 13 of the Companies Act, 2013, approved an alteration of Clause III(A) (Main Objects) of the Memorandum of Association, broadening the permitted scope of business to include, inter alia, furniture and interior solutions, human and pet nutrition products, solar and renewable energy solutions, cosmetics and personal care products, advertising and media services, artist and event management, and information technology and software development services. Management states this 'provides the Company with the flexibility to pursue future business opportunities in these sectors as and when considered commercially viable, while continuing its existing business operations' — i.e. it creates optionality only, with no project, site, investment amount or timeline attached. The Company remains a textile trading business (cloth and grey fabrics) with one permanent employee as on 31st March 2026 and no holding, subsidiary, joint venture or associate company.
currentContext.mdna: India remaining one of the fastest-growing major economies in FY2025-26, supported by robust domestic demand, infrastructure development, policy reforms, digitalisation and favourable demographics.|Government initiatives — Make in India, Digital India, Startup India, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes, PM Gati Shakti and renewable energy policies — encouraging industrial growth, manufacturing, exports and entrepreneurship.|Increasing demand for consumer products, lifestyle products and organised retail.|Growing renewable energy and solar power market.|Rising awareness towards health, nutrition, wellness and personal care products.|Increasing digitalisation and demand for software and IT-enabled services; growth in advertising, branding, media and event management services.|Infrastructure development and increasing demand for warehousing and logistics services.|Management's stated view that businesses with diversified operations and adaptable business models are expected to benefit from changing global market dynamics.

risks.note: The Chairman's message states the Company 'continues to operate in the textile trading business, primarily engaged in the trading of cloth and grey fabrics, which remains its principal line of business'. All revenue-generating activity therefore sits in one low-value-add trading line; the newly added objects are optionality only and none is described as operational.

risks.risk: Economic slowdown and fluctuations in consumer demand
risks.note: Flagged first in the MD&A 'CHALLENGES' list of business risks the Company monitors. As a trading intermediary the Company has no contracted order book or pipeline disclosed, so demand swings pass through directly.
Explicitly listed under MD&A CHALLENGES. Cloth and grey-fabric trading is a fragmented, low-barrier activity and the report evidences no brand, distribution, cost or technology moat.

risks.risk: Volatility in raw material and commodity prices
risks.note: Explicitly listed under MD&A CHALLENGES; for a fabric trader, input price swings act directly on inventory value and trading spread.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the diversification into unrelated sectors
risks.note: The Members altered Clause III(A) (Main Objects) of the MoA at the AGM of 16th September 2025 to permit furniture and interior solutions, human and pet nutrition, solar and renewable energy, cosmetics and personal care, advertising and media, artist and event management and IT/software development. Management commits only to evaluating these 'as and when considered commercially viable' — no project, capital plan, partner or timeline is disclosed, and the Company had one permanent employee on its rolls as on 31st March 2026.

Listed under MD&A CHALLENGES. The report also records that Corporate Governance provisions under Regulation 15(2) of SEBI LODR are currently not applicable because paid-up equity capital is below Rs 10 crore and net worth below Rs 25 crore — i.e. several governance obligations bind the Company only voluntarily today, and would attach if it crosses those thresholds.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruptions and logistics challenges
risks.note: Explicitly listed under MD&A CHALLENGES; a trading model depends on third-party supply and movement of goods it does not control.

Explicitly listed under MD&A CHALLENGES and repeated in the Cautionary Statement as a factor that could cause actual results to differ materially, although no export or import exposure is quantified anywhere in the routed text.

risks.risk: Rapid technological change and cybersecurity / IT risk
risks.note: Both are listed under MD&A CHALLENGES, and are material principally to the newly permitted software, IT-enabled services and media objects rather than to the existing trading line.
